summary: Closure review: references/numbering requirements appear satisfied, but the mandatory Disclosure Statement still includes run-level file paths and full SHA‑256 hashes and therefore remains non‑compliant with the track's concise‑disclosure requirement. Accept_for_finalisation is false until the Disclosure is condensed as specified below.
critical_issues: Disclosure Statement contains run-level file paths and full SHA‑256 hashes (e.g., execution/raw_results.jsonl, provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256) and duplicates execution-log material in ordinary manuscript prose; this violates the track's concise Disclosure requirement and must be remediated.
required_revisions: Condense the Disclosure Statement into a single concise paragraph reporting only the mandatory items: LLM(s) used and model identifiers, orchestration/adapter framework, canonical verifier identifier, existence of a preregistration (study id), that artifacts/manifests are archived (name the manifest and provide at most a single manifest-level checksum), the autonomy-lock boundary (human-selected topic and pre-lock collaboration vs. post-lock autonomous execution), and an explicit statement that no human manually edited the manuscript after the lock. Remove file-level paths, per‑episode filenames, and full SHA‑256 hashes from the Disclosure prose; refer readers to the archived execution manifest (named) for low‑level provenance and audit details.
optional_revisions: Add one brief sentence in Methods clarifying that model_configuration.json records temperature = null and that null indicates provider‑default sampling semantics (not evidence of deterministic sampling).

If space permits, add a short paragraph in Discussion contrasting how an independent‑generation arm or a repair‑enabled arm would change the estimand and enable non‑degenerate inference, citing the archived sensitivity scripts/artifacts.
